english: Let $x,y,z$ be positive real numbers such that $x+4y+9z=18$, and let $A$ and $H$ denote the arithmetic mean and the harmonic mean of $x,y,z$, respectively. Then the value of $A\cdot H$ at the point $(x,y,z)$ at which $H$ attains its greatest value is ______.
hindi: माना $x,y,z$ ऐसी धनात्मक वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं कि $x+4y+9z=18$ है, तथा $A$ और $H$ क्रमशः $x,y,z$ के समान्तर माध्य और हरात्मक माध्य हैं। तब जिस बिन्दु $(x,y,z)$ पर $H$ अपना अधिकतम मान प्राप्त करता है, उस पर $A\cdot H$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $H=\dfrac{3}{\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z}$, so $H$ is greatest when $\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z$ is least
(Same bound by AM-GM: the product is $14+\left(\frac{4y}x+\frac xy\right)+\left(\frac{9z}x+\frac xz\right)+\left(\frac{9z}y+\frac{4y}z\right)\ge14+4+6+12$)
solution_full: $H=\dfrac{3}{\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z}$, so $H$ is greatest exactly when $\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z$ is least under $x+4y+9z=18$.

Take the vectors $\left(\sqrt x,2\sqrt y,3\sqrt z\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt x},\dfrac1{\sqrt y},\dfrac1{\sqrt z}\right)$. Their dot product is $1+2+3=6$, so by Cauchy-Schwarz $36\le(x+4y+9z)\left(\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z\right)=18\left(\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z\right)$.

The same bound follows from AM-GM: expanding, $(x+4y+9z)\left(\dfrac1x+\dfrac1y+\dfrac1z\right)=14+\left(\dfrac{4y}{x}+\dfrac{x}{y}\right)+\left(\dfrac{9z}{x}+\dfrac{x}{z}\right)+\left(\dfrac{9z}{y}+\dfrac{4y}{z}\right)\ge14+4+6+12=36$.
Equality holds iff the vectors are parallel, i.e. $\sqrt x\cdot\sqrt x=2\sqrt y\cdot\sqrt y=3\sqrt z\cdot\sqrt z$, that is, $x=2y=3z$ (the same as the AM-GM equality conditions).
With $x=k$, $y=\dfrac k2$, $z=\dfrac k3$: $k+2k+3k=18$, so $k=3$ and the point is $\left(3,\dfrac32,1\right)$, where $H=\dfrac32$.
At this point $A=\dfrac{3+\frac32+1}{3}=\dfrac{11}{6}$, so $A\cdot H=\dfrac{11}{6}\cdot\dfrac32=\dfrac{11}{4}=2.75$. (Consistently, $A\ge G\ge H$: $G=\sqrt[3]{4.5}\approx1.65$.)
originality_note: New: the harmonic mean of three numbers is maximised under a weighted linear constraint; the Titu/Cauchy-Schwarz bound (or the pairwise AM-GM expansion) gives the optimum point x = 2y = 3z, and the answer combines two means at that point (way 5: relation between means linked with a weighted extremum). Closest known: '(a + b + c)(1/a + 1/b + 1/c) >= 9' (AM-HM). Different because: the constraint is weighted, so the optimum is not at x = y = z, and the asked quantity A.H needs the exact optimal point.
